payload.goal:
Add order priority and backorders to this warehouse codebase, across every layer that already exists.

Domain  - src/domain/orders.ts:
- Export type OrderPriority = "standard" | "express".
- Order gains a readonly priority field of that type. It is optional at the call site: an order placed without a priority is treated as "standard", so existing callers keep working unchanged.
- placeOrder throws OrderError when a priority is supplied and is neither "standard" nor "express".
- Export interface Backorder with readonly orderId, skuId and missing fields, where missing is a positive integer.
- WarehouseState gains a readonly backorders field keyed by order id.
- reserveOrder records a Backorder for every line whose quantity exceeds the available units, instead of throwing, and leaves the order in a status from which it can still be cancelled.
- Export listBackorders(state) returning every recorded Backorder.

Application  - src/application/warehouse-service.ts:
- The service exposes the new operations and emits a warehouse event for a recorded backorder.

Fulfillment  - src/fulfillment/planner.ts:
- Within one wave, planFulfillment lists express orders before standard ones. Its existing signature does not change.

Durability  - src/durability/journal.ts:
- HistoryAnalytics gains a backorders count derived from the events.

API  - src/api/server.ts:
- The server exposes the backorders of the current state.

Presentation  - src/presentation/tower.ts:
- The rendered SVG distinguishes express orders from standard ones.

Probe  - src/probe/g6.ts and a package script named study:g6-probe:
- Follow the shape of the existing probes: export main() returning a JSON string, and write exactly one JSON object to stdout when invoked directly, with no other output.
- Two invocations from the same commit must emit byte-identical output.

Preserve all existing behaviour and keep every existing test passing. Put new tests next to the code they cover, inside the directories the test script already scans.

scripts.test: node --test src/domain/*.test.ts src/probe/*.test.ts src/scenarios/*.test.ts src/application/*.test.ts src/presentation/*.test.ts src/api/*.test.ts src/fulfillment/*.test.ts src/durability/*.test.ts

root.title: Priority and backorder rollout
root.objective: Add order priority and backorder support across the existing warehouse stack without breaking current behavior.
expectedOutcomes: Existing callers can omit priority and get standard behavior.
Invalid supplied priorities fail fast in the domain.
Unavailable reserve quantities produce recorded backorders instead of hard failure.
Express orders are planned before standard orders within the same wave.
Journal analytics can count backorders from the event history.
The server exposes current backorders and the tower SVG distinguishes express orders.
The g6 probe emits stable one-object JSON with no extra output.

complexitySignals.rationale: The change crosses several existing layer contracts and adds one new probe path, but each leaf stays independently verifiable.

cut.rationale: The work splits by stable layer contracts and verification surfaces, not by file count or mechanical path grouping.

children.title: Order priority and backorders in domain
children.objective: Extend order modeling, validation, reservation, and backorder listing in the domain layer.
expectedOutcomes: OrderPriority is exported as standard or express.
Orders default to standard when priority is omitted.
Supplying any other priority raises OrderError.
WarehouseState includes backorders keyed by order id.
Reservation records backorders for shortages and preserves cancellation eligibility.
listBackorders returns every recorded Backorder.

children.title: Warehouse service backorder flow
children.objective: Expose the new service operations and emit a warehouse event when a backorder is recorded.
expectedOutcomes: The warehouse service surfaces the new backorder-aware operations.
Recording a backorder emits the corresponding warehouse event.
Existing service behavior remains intact for non-backorder cases.

children.title: Express-first fulfillment planning
children.objective: Keep the existing planner signature and sort express orders before standard orders within a wave.
expectedOutcomes: planFulfillment keeps its current signature.
Within one wave, express orders are listed before standard orders.
No unrelated fulfillment behavior changes.

children.title: Journal backorder analytics
children.objective: Derive a backorders count in history analytics from recorded events.
expectedOutcomes: HistoryAnalytics includes a backorders count.
The count is derived from events already in the journal.
Existing analytics remain unchanged apart from the added count.

children.title: API backorder exposure
children.objective: Expose the current state's backorders through the server surface.
expectedOutcomes: The server response includes the current state's backorders.
The exposure is consistent with the domain state shape.
Existing API behavior is preserved.

children.title: Priority-aware tower rendering
children.objective: Render express orders distinctly from standard orders in the SVG output.
expectedOutcomes: The tower SVG distinguishes express orders from standard orders.
The visual distinction does not alter unrelated rendering behavior.
Existing presentation tests continue to pass.
